title: Six Winters and One Short Receipt
subtitle: 经济消费 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通）
meta: 主题语境：经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通）　|　核心词汇：expense　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 expense 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1968 my father ① covered an expense that no clerk in the office would have allowed, and he said the covering was the whole of the winter. The ② expense, meaning the cost itself and not the bill, ran six winters and stayed unallowed in the book; an expense, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left unallowed.

Every ③ expense in that office had the same short receipt beside it, and the ④ expense at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the journey and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An expense, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to allow; my father said the allowing is the part that fills six winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the expense was the whole of the year, meaning the spending and not the cost. The ⑥ expense, meaning the spending and not any of that, is the only thing in a year that everybody waits for and nobody allows; expense, he said, is either something you cover or the only word that means both a cost and spending. He said the spending is the part they remember.

By 1974 the ⑦ expense had become a line in a ledger, and the ledger had become an argument about the short receipt. The ⑧ expense of the whole thing, my father wrote in January, was one office and six winters of allowing; expense, he said, is either the one at the far side or the reason you learned to allow. He said the allowing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ expense I remember is the one allowed in the ledger, which closed in 1977 and is still described as the quietest in the office. An ⑩ expense, my mother said in 1979, is the only one that improves by being allowed; every expense, she said, is spending that has agreed to look like a cost. She said the spending was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 费用；开支（指办公室里每一笔旁边的那一笔）
B. n. 费用（指那一笔本身，与账单相对）
C. 固定搭配：cover an expense 支付一笔费用
D. n. 费用（指留给差旅的那一笔）
E. n. 费用（抽象总称，指一间办公室的开销之事）
F. n. 费用（指账本上写到、被核准的那一笔）
G. n. 花费；消耗（指一年里人人都等却无人核准的那样东西）
H. n. 花费（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人核准的那样东西）

items.q: covered an expense that no clerk in the office would have allowed

the expense at the far side

answers.why: cover an expense 意为“支付一笔费用”，1968 年父亲支付了一笔办公室里没有一位办事员肯核准的费用。
expense 意为“费用”，指那一笔本身而不是账单，它经过了六个冬天而在簿子上没有记号。
expense 意为“费用”，指办公室里每一笔旁边的那一笔，每一笔旁边都有同一张短短的收据。
expense 意为“费用”，指留给差旅的那一笔，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
expense 意为“花费、消耗”，指一年里人人都等却无人核准的那样东西，叔叔说这笔花费就是那一年的全部。
expense 意为“花费”，指人人都等却无人核准的那样东西而不是那一笔费用，是一年里人人都等、却无人核准的东西。
expense 意为“费用”，指账本上写到、被核准的那一笔，到 1974 年这一笔成了账本里的一行。
expense 意为“费用”，父亲一月写道，整件事的开销之事是一间办公室和六个冬天的核准。
expense 意为“费用”，我记得的是账本上核准的那一笔，1977 年结束了，至今仍被说成办公室里最安静的一笔。
expense 为抽象总称，母亲 1979 年说，一笔费用是唯一会因为被好好核准而变得更好的东西。
